incidents.name: VerusBridge
incidents.notes: Verus submitImports accepted a crafted partialtransactionproof/MMR proof that bypassed VerusProof validation, minting fake ETH/tBTC/USDC imports.

sources.ref: onchain review: 0x71518580f36feceffe0721f06ba4703218cd7f63 is the Verus Delegator, an unverified module-registry proxy that delegatecalls an address[] of 11 module contracts and emits no upgrade event at all, so the code history was recovered in Tier 2 by binary-searching eth_getStorageAt over the array (length slot 13 = 11, data at keccak256(13)+i) between creation block 18272987 (2023-10-03) and each incident block. Last change per module before incident 1 (block 25118335): contracts[7] 2023-11-03T17:11:11Z (block 18492941), contracts[2] 2024-03-21T22:05:59Z (block 19485889), contracts[9] 2024-12-07T20:40:35Z (block 21353057), contracts[10] 2024-12-07T20:43:47Z (block 21353072), contracts[5] 2026-01-09T20:55:35Z (block 24199650) and contracts[0]/[1]/[6]/[8] 2026-02-28T16:29:47Z (block 24556629, tx 0xc17ab86af35ac0f37a3001e249ba8176e53189151601d50eddc427cacf11ddba from the Verus upgrade signer 0x896e59efcbec700bc9f447af7018bdc5ca1fa5ab, selector 0x60cd61a5); contracts[3] and [4] were untouched since deployment. Age measured from the latest of those, 2026-02-28, rather than the 2023 Delegator deployment

incidents.documentedLastChange: 2026-02-28T16:29:47Z (block 24556629, tx 0xc17ab86af35ac0f37a3001e249ba8176e53189151601d50eddc427cacf11ddba): last delegate-contract swap on the Verus Delegator before the incident, recovered by binary-searching eth_getStorageAt over the contracts address[] (length slot 13, data at keccak256(13)+i); that upgrade replaced contracts[0], [1], [6] and [8]

incidents.name: VerusBridge duplicate-state-root parser divergence
incidents.notes: The bridge accepted notarization bytes whose duplicate state-root entries were interpreted differently by Verus and Ethereum, installing an attacker-chosen root and authorizing unbacked imports.

sources.ref: onchain review: same Verus Delegator 0x71518580f36feceffe0721f06ba4703218cd7f63 as the 2026-05-17 incident; because it emits no upgrade event the code history was recovered in Tier 2 by binary-searching eth_getStorageAt over the contracts address[] (length slot 13, data at keccak256(13)+i) between creation block 18272987 and incident block 25592836. After the May incident every module was replaced twice: contracts[3], [4] and [7] on 2026-07-08T14:57:23Z (block 25488591, tx 0xdcd9821ff75561c03f85673d992ad988f7d067caf1f3df581ac54303537ff84a) and contracts[0], [1], [2], [5], [6], [8], [9], [10] on 2026-07-12T16:57:35Z (block 25517881, tx 0xb29f45f3c788cc635fe746754dfe79b00f36758cbd9f418e69866e72c08e192d), both from the Verus upgrade signer 0x896e59efcbec700bc9f447af7018bdc5ca1fa5ab with selector 0x60cd61a5. Age measured from the 2026-07-12 swap, 10.5 days before the exploit, rather than the 2023 Delegator deployment

incidents.documentedLastChange: 2026-07-12T16:57:35Z (block 25517881, tx 0xb29f45f3c788cc635fe746754dfe79b00f36758cbd9f418e69866e72c08e192d): last delegate-contract swap on the Verus Delegator before the incident, recovered by binary-searching eth_getStorageAt over the contracts address[] (length slot 13, data at keccak256(13)+i); it replaced 8 of the 11 modules four days after the 2026-07-08 post-hack redeploy (block 25488591)
